claim_text: RMSNorm divides each coordinate by the root mean square of the vector, so a larger epsilon stops that division from shri

spec.explain: Toy curve of RMSNorm gain from 1910.07467: watch the gain number, the RMS-rescaled size that big values keep after division.

questions.q: Set r to 0.1: what happens to the gain? Do you expect a large activation to lose more gain than a small one?
questions.why: Tests the misconception that epsilon shrinks big values more.

questions.q: Set eps to 1: what happens to the gain?
questions.why: Reads the regime point where eps equals r squared.

questions.q: Set r to 2: what happens to the gain?
Set eps to 0.01: what happens to the gain?
questions.why: Reads near-unity gain when epsilon is tiny.
